Determine chemical composition of the Fe-9Al AIMFC ingot (Al, Si, Mn, S, C, O, H, N).

characterization_methods.key_findings: UTS 349 ± 6.3 MPa, YS 318 ± 8.0 MPa, EL total 0.1 ± 0.1%; Fe-9Al AIMFC failed at very low stress levels during tensile test without significant elongation.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; each tensile data point average of three tests.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure room-temperature tensile properties (UTS, YS, EL) of hot-rolled Fe-9Al AIMFC.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: microcrack formation due to hydrogen embrittlement
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Microcracks were observed in hot-rolled Fe-9Al AIMFC plates; attributed to hydrogen embrittlement from the high residual hydrogen concentration in the as-cast ingots (H 0.0052 wt.%).

interfaces.interface_notes: Single-phase Fe-Al solid solution; no phase interfaces reported. Fe-9Al AIMFC ingots were completely free from gas porosity but exhibited microcracks.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: room-temperature tensile ductility (total elongation) and hot-workability
comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: Fe-9Al AIMFC failed at very low stress during the room-temperature tensile test without significant elongation (EL 0.1 ± 0.1%), whereas Fe-9Al VIM exhibited about 9% total elongation; the hot-working response of Fe-9Al AIMFC was poor with microcracks in hot-rolled plates.

processing_steps.atmosphere: air, with protective flux cover (Al2O3, CaO, MgO, CaF2)
processing_steps.method: air induction melting with flux cover (AIMFC)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 30-kg heats of Fe-9 wt.% Al were prepared by Inductotherm medium-frequency AIM of 50-kg capacity; commercial purity Al and Fe used; iron charge cleaned by pickling in dilute hydrochloric acid and charged into an alumina-lined crucible; preheated flux (Al2O3, CaO, MgO, CaF2) added after iron melting; cleaned/preheated aluminum plunged into molten iron; melt top poured into split cast iron molds.
80-mm-diameter AIMFC ingots preheated in a hearth furnace at 1373 K for 1 h and hot-forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature.
24-mm-thick forged billet sections preheated at 1373 K for 1 h and hot rolled 50% with 1-mm reduction per pass; samples reheated after every six rolling passes; final thickness 12 mm.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: hot-rolled Fe-9Al AIMFC; each hardness data point is an average of five measurements; each tensile data point is an average of three tests.

phases_present.phase_name: disordered Fe-Al solid solution (α-Fe(Al)) with expected short-range ordering

structures.overall_structure: Annealed, coarse-grained microstructure after hot rolling; large polygonal grains with moderate dark pitting and clear grain boundaries.

unmapped_findings: Fe-9Al AIMFC as-cast ingots were completely free from gas porosity but exhibited microcracks (unlike Fe-7Al AIMFC ingots, which were free from microcracks); the microcracks are attributed to hydrogen embrittlement from the higher hydrogen concentration in the Fe-9Al AIMFC ingots (H 0.0052 wt.% in Table I).

The hot-working response of Fe-9Al AIMFC was poor, in contrast to the excellent hot workability of the same alloy produced by VIM; microcracks were observed in hot-rolled plates and may persist even after hot working.
Fe-9Al AIMFC failed at very low stress levels during the room-temperature tensile test without exhibiting any significant elongation, whereas Fe-9Al VIM exhibited about 9% total elongation.

Fe-9Al AIMFC ingots exhibited a higher hydrogen concentration (0.0052 wt.%) than Fe-9Al VIM (0.0021 wt.%), attributed to hydrogen pick-up during pouring/solidification exposure to the atmosphere and the higher aluminum level.
Aluminum recovery during AIMFC was 95–98%, comparable to VIM (96–98%); the recovery applies to Fe-7Al and Fe-9Al AIMFC melts.
